Four forms evade it. **Omission** — a construction that leaves a defaulted seam out names nothing forbidden — is first, because it is the one that actually shipped (F1); it is closed for the three fixtures that can drive readiness and nowhere else, since requiring the parameter at all 37 executor constructions would be churn. **Spelling rather than route** (cycle-2 C5, recorded rather than fixed): the readiness-fixture rule matches files that write `.showPermissionReadiness`, so a fixture resolving the same operation through `AgentOperation(rawValue: "show_permission_readiness")` is not in the matched set and never was — the cycle-2 review built exactly that file and watched every pin pass. **PR #72 CYCLE-1 FIX ROUND (review at `4a6ea14`; fixes at `b29fed9`).** Eleven items, all fixed in branch. Disposition by finding:

**F1 (HIGH, fixed) — the branch did not close finding 1.** `AgentRunnerTests` carries its own `makeExecutor`, unrelated to `AgentActionExecutorTests`', and it built an `AgentActionExecutor` without `permissionReadinessService`, so it took the production default. `tierZeroCommandAutoRunsWithoutApprovalDecision` drives a `.showPermissionReadiness` plan through it, reaching `PermissionReadinessCapabilityAdapter` and calling `currentStatus` — three live `AXIsProcessTrusted()` and `AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus` reads per run. The scan's doc comment now lists omission first among its evasions, names this incident as the instance that shipped, and points at the probe as the method that does enumerate.

**The probe, because it is the durable technique.** Patch each live checker to print a marker and return the real answer, run the whole suite with `--no-parallel`, and count. This is an enumeration, not a battery — the mutants must survive, and the log is the measurement. Run at `2aeb699`: **zero markers** on the microphone read, on `AXIsProcessTrusted()` and on `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()`, with all three suites passing 1383/107. A zero count from a broken probe looks identical to a clean sweep, so a positive control was run alongside: the same marker on `microphoneStatus()`, the caller every readiness test reaches, fired **23 times** across the readiness tests including `tierZeroCommandAutoRunsWithoutApprovalDecision` — which confirms both that the mechanism works and that F1's fix routes that test through the deterministic service rather than removing its readiness call.

**F1's class, closed at proportionate cost.** Requiring the parameter at all 37 executor constructions in the suite would be churn, since most never touch a readiness path. `everyExecutorFixtureThatCanDriveReadinessInjectsTheSeam` takes the narrow rule instead: a file that both builds an `AgentActionExecutor` and names `.showPermissionReadiness` is one plan away from a live read. Exactly three files match, the test pins that count so a rule that stopped matching anything fails rather than passing forever, and `EgressClassificationTests` — the third — gained the injection it was missing.

**F3 (fixed) — the scan was fail-open on partial injection.** The forbidden list held `PermissionReadinessService()` with its parentheses, so a call naming `screenPermissionChecker` and leaving `microphonePermissionChecker` at its live default matched nothing. Both checkers are defaulted, so *any* direct construction can be partial and the only safe rule is that tests never call the initializer: the token lost its closing parenthesis and the helper's own file became the single target-qualified exemption, itself bounded by a test asserting that file constructs exactly one service, inside `deterministic`, naming both checkers. The review's other note in that area is fixed too — the `files.count > 20` floor sat three above one target's real 23 and would have tripped on an ordinary consolidation, so the empty-scan guard now names the files it expects to find instead of counting them.

**F4 and F5 (fixed) — two invariants that were requests, not mechanisms.** Both twin headers said "keep the two in step" and nothing enforced it: deleting the grants-on-request flip from the **core** copy survived the whole suite, because nothing in that target reads it, while the same deletion in the app copy dies by `ScreenAccessOnboardingTests`. The gate had the same shape — inverting `geteuid() != 0` survived, three tests silently stopped running, and the suite reported green with the total dropping 1377 → 1374 and nobody told. `TwinnedTestSupportTests` holds both: the class bodies and the trait files are compared with comment lines stripped (the copies differ in prose on purpose), the predicate is pinned as source text because a skip cannot be observed from inside the run that was skipped, and a fourth test ties the gate to its reason relationally — it fails both when a new directory-locking test arrives ungated and when a gate is deleted. **This matters more here than it would elsewhere: there is no CI in this repository, so the gate has never fired anywhere and nothing but these pins checks it.**

**F6 (fixed) — two tautologies, and the branch's only new compiler warnings.** `#expect(SystemScreenCapturePermissionChecker() is any ScreenCapturePermissionChecking)` is true by declaration, and the compiler said so twice (`warning: 'is' test is always true`). Both are gone; the useful half — the source-text check that catches a rename in `Sources/` — stays and gained a check that every token in the list still names something real. The related survivor is closed as well: neutering the scan's inner loop so it inspected nothing survived the whole suite, so the matching rule is now a pure function pinned against a fixture covering partial injection, prose in comments, and the trailing-comment case the narrower `grep -v "//"` would drop. A cold build at the fix head reports **six** warning sites, all pre-existing and all in `Tests/`; this branch adds none.

**F2 and the record corrections (all applied above, in place).** F2's false premise, the nine-files count, the `AudioCommandRecorder` reasoning and the "member for member" overstatement are each corrected where this entry wrote them. The containment doc comment's claim that both middle guards are documented where they sit is corrected in `Sources/` too: the iteration cap's rationale lives on `VisionSessionLimits.maximumIterations`, not at its call site.

**Fix-round battery: 7 mutants, 7 killed at `b29fed9`** (logs `.build/mutate/b29fed9-20260819T153*`), one per finding, each reverting the fix so the new pin has something to catch — **N1** F1's injection dropped → `everyExecutorFixtureThatCanDriveReadinessInjectsTheSeam`; **N7** a real partial injection in `ScreenCaptureServiceTests` → `noTestSourceConstructsALivePermissionChecker`; **N2** the token narrowed back → three tests; **N3** the matching loop neutered → two; **N4** the core twin's flip deleted → `theTwinnedPermissionStubsAreTheSameCode`; **N5** the gate inverted → two; **N6** a gate tag removed → `theGateCoversExactlyTheTestsThatForceAFilesystemFailure`. **N1, N4, N5 and N7 were measured survivors before this round.** The branch's original seven were rerun at the same SHA and are still 7/7.

Same section-D class as findings 1 and 2, a different seam, and not named by this ticket — filed as its own ticket rather than absorbed.

**PR #72 CYCLE-2 FIX ROUND (review at `b9b2b83`; fixes at `e9ec5b9`).** **Nothing in this round is a defect in the shipped tree** — the review says so in its own verdict, and re-measured it: no live read exists at `b9b2b83`, and every cycle-1 pin catches the mutation it was written for. **A method upgrade, worth keeping.** The cycle-1 *fix round* proved the marker probe worked with a *positive* control on the caller. That shows the printing mechanism works; it does not show the three probes were wired to call sites that would ever fire. The cycle-2 *review* added the negative control: the identical three probes re-run at `4a6ea14`, the pre-fix head, produce **3 markers each, all under `tierZeroCommandAutoRunsWithoutApprovalDecision`**. Same probe, same call site, same plan — it fires when a live read exists and is silent now. A zero is only evidence when the same instrument has been seen to register a one.

**C1 (fixed) — `.init()` walked a live service past every pin.** `permissionReadinessService: .init()` is `PermissionReadinessService.init()` with both checkers left at their live defaults, and it survived at `b9b2b83` — putting a live service back at the exact fixture whose live reads were F1. Nothing caught it: the token scan looks for `PermissionReadinessService(`, which that line does not spell, and the fixture rule asked only whether the file *contained* the identifier, which it does, in that very line. **Checking a parameter's name is not checking its value.** The fixture rule now requires the injected form, and a new rule requires every value handed to a `permissionReadinessService:` parameter anywhere in either target to be `.deterministic(...)` or a same-named forwarded parameter — which closes the spelling class rather than the one site. Three mutants prove it: the same `.init()` at the F1 call site, at `makeExecutor`'s default, and in `VisionTestContext`, all dead.

**C2 (fixed) — the gate pin never tied a gate to its test.** It counted locks and tags across the tree and compared totals, so moving `@Test(.requiresUnprivilegedProcess)` off a directory-locking test onto its neighbour left both counts at four and the suite green, with one forced-failure test silently ungated. **A comparison of two aggregates is not a statement about any member of either.** Each file is now segmented at its `@Test` lines and the two facts must agree inside every segment. Both directions are pinned and both are real: a lock without a gate fails on a root runner for a reason that is not a defect, and a gate without a lock silently stops running a test that never needed gating. Treated as a merge accident rather than an adversarial one, because an attribute landing on the wrong function is what an inserted test does.

**C3 (fixed, and it was a contained edit) — the class body is not the whole type.** Adding `extension DeterministicScreenPermissions { ... }` to the app twin alone left both compared bodies byte-identical and the suite green, while the twins had genuinely diverged. Extending the type is now refused outright anywhere in either target, which keeps every member inside the class body where the drift comparison can see it. Recorded from the review because it bounds the pin honestly: comment lines, blank lines, indentation and whitespace runs are normalized away, so reformatting is not false drift, but member *order* is not normalized — the surviving lines are joined in order and compared as strings.

**C4 (fixed, and it was one enumerator) — the scans read one directory deep; SwiftPM compiles a target's `path:` recursively.** A file at `Tests/MacAgentCoreTests/<anything>/Live.swift` was compiled into the target and invisible to every pin. Latent, since no subdirectory exists under either target, and closed rather than recorded because the fix is a recursive enumerator in one shared helper (`TestSourceTree`) that both scan suites now use. Proved by planting exactly that file: the build log shows `Compiling MacAgentCoreTests ZZLive.swift` and the scan reports it as `MacAgentCoreTests/ZZSubdirProbe/ZZLive.swift:6`, where before the round it passed. The same helper qualifies each suite's self-exemption by target path rather than by basename, so a same-named file in the other target is no longer skipped along with it.

**C5 (recorded, deliberately not fixed).** The readiness-fixture rule keys on how the operation is *spelled*, not on the route it takes: a fixture resolving `AgentOperation(rawValue: "show_permission_readiness")` is not in its matched set, and the cycle-2 review built that file, ran a readiness plan through a seamless executor, and watched every pin pass. Its count pin does catch an *existing* matched file that stops spelling the symbol (measured). **Hardening a text scan against every spelling is not a finite task**, and the method that does enumerate — the marker probe — already exists and is recorded. Written into the scan's own doc comment beside the omission and indirection admissions, and into the known-limitations list above.

**C6 (fixed) — two lines the cycle-1 round left stale, both contradicted by the same entry.** The scan was still described as forbidding "the argument-free `PermissionReadinessService()`" twenty lines above the F3 paragraph explaining why the parenthesis was dropped, and a test-support target was still called "the only way to get literally one copy" after F2 established the cheaper dependency edge. Both corrected in place, along with the evasion list, which predated the scan's own doc comment. The rest of the entry was swept for the same class of staleness; nothing else was found.

**Cycle-2 battery: 6 mutants, 6 killed at `e9ec5b9`** — **A3, A2 and A1 were the review's own measured survivors**, rebuilt from its descriptions: **A3** `.init()` at the F1 fixture → two tests; **A3b** and **A3c** the same spelling at a fixture default and in `VisionTestContext` → `everyReadinessServiceArgumentIsTheDeterministicHelper`; **A2** a lock losing its gate and **A2b** a gate landing on a test that locks nothing → `everyDirectoryLockingTestCarriesTheGateAndNoOtherTestDoes`, the two halves of the move the review measured; **A1** an extension on the app twin alone → `neitherTwinIsExtendedOutsideItsClassBody`. C4 is proved by the planted file rather than by a mutant, since no mutation of existing text can create one.

**A correction that took three passes, and the lesson is none of the first two.** This paragraph has now been wrong twice in the same direction: both drafts blamed a review session for an error that was the coordinator's. The first read the five-versus-six warning-site gap as a session's miscount and generalised it into a pattern; the second retracted that but still opened with "cycle 1 quoted five". **Cycle 1 quoted no such thing.** Neither wrong mechanism is restated here — a wrong diagnosis left in circulation is worse than none.

**Where "five" actually came from, enumerated.** Cycle 1's review comment, cycle 1's fix-round comment and the PR body all say **six**; so does this entry's own cycle-1 section, and that section's line is the *only* warning-site line the changelog carried before the cycle-2 record commit — `b9b2b83` has one and it says six, while `33c5866`, `81416e2`, `4a6ea14` and `b29fed9` have none at all. The first "five" anywhere on this branch is in this paragraph's own first draft, at `a70b01a`. It reached the branch through **the coordinator's cycle-2 review prompt**, and through nothing else.

**And the five was never wrong either.** SONNY-169 measured five sites at `1002d82` and, in the same ticket, *predicted* a sixth arriving with row D at `Tests/MacAgentTests/TaskDeletePresentationTests.swift:88`. That file did not exist at `1002d82` — `git cat-file -e 1002d82:Tests/MacAgentTests/TaskDeletePresentationTests.swift` fails — and arrived through PR #67 (`c733212`), added by `176e618` on `feature/task-history-controls`. Line 88 on `main` today is `let realID = try? #require(record.id)`: exactly the predicted sixth. Re-measured rather than taken on trust — a cold build in a detached worktree at `1002d82` emits **five**, precisely the five SONNY-169 listed; a cold build at `ef6a326` and at this branch's heads emits **six**, those same five plus the new one. **Five and six are both correct measurements, of different trees.** No session miscounted, no count on this branch was reported before its population was fixed, and the branch adds zero warning sites — which was never in question.

**The cause, narrower than either wrong diagnosis and worth more than both:** a measurement was repeated without the SHA it was taken at. This repository already requires every measurement to carry one, and this is what it costs when a quotation drops it — not a wrong number, but a *true* number that reads as a contradiction of another true number, with each session downstream inventing a defect to explain a gap that was never there. The rule's stated reason is that a bare count cannot be told apart from a stale one; this adds the sharper case, that it cannot be told apart from a correct one of a *different tree* either. And the second-order lesson, earned the hard way across three passes: **when a claim's provenance is wrong, correcting the claim is not enough — the attribution has to be checked against what each party actually said**, or the retraction inherits the misattribution it was written to undo. The failure and the fix both live in prose, not in code; no test could have caught any of it, and none was added.

Behavior added:
- `scripts/mutate <plan>` runs a mutation battery and **refuses to start while `git status --porcelain` prints anything**, on every command, with no override flag. That refusal is the ticket; everything else is convenience.
- It reverts each mutant from a byte-exact copy taken before the mutation rather than from HEAD, including from its `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` trap, so an interrupted run leaves no mutant in the tree and no revert can reach past the file it mutated.
- It refuses a mutant whose `from` text does not match exactly once — zero matches or two — before any test runs; aborts on a red baseline; reports a survivor loudly and exits 2 for it; distinguishes a compiler kill from a test kill; names the killing tests; and stamps the SHA on the report.

Behavior preserved (required, no blanket claims): nothing existing was touched, and that is a checkable claim rather than a blanket one. `scripts/mutate` is standalone — it does not source `scripts/lib/signing.sh`, and `scripts/plane`, `scripts/package-app.sh`, `scripts/create-signing-identity.sh` and `scripts/lib/` are byte-identical to their `4894fcb` versions. `.claude/hooks/verify-tests-before-stop.sh` still fires on Swift changes and is unaffected: this branch changes no Swift. The full suite was rerun anyway and matches the branch point at 1373 in 104.

Architectural decisions / pitfalls discovered (required, write "none" if true):
- **The count was four in the ticket and it is five.** SONNY-75's description records two occurrences, its 2026-08-16 triage comment adds SONNY-83 as the third, and its 2026-08-17 coordinator update adds SONNY-161 and PR #67's cycle-3 fix round while numbering them three and four — silently dropping SONNY-83. Sweeping the changelog for the incident itself (`grep -n uncommitted` filtered to battery/mutation/checkout lines) finds three distinct branch entries — **`feature/workspace-restriction-scope`, `feature/prebuilt-plan-dispatch` and `feature/app-catalog-dissolution`** — and SONNY-161's is in its own closing comment, verified by reading it back rather than inferring it; PR #67's is recorded only in the coordinator's comment, quoting the session. Five, and the script says five. **The coordinator confirmed the correction on the ticket** and recorded how the wrong number was produced — inferred from "the description said twice, I knew of two more" rather than counted — which is the same failure SONNY-167 was filed for, by the same author, earlier the same day.
- **Two near neighbours are deliberately not counted**, so the number stays checkable: `feature/full-repo-correctness-review`'s is a scratch-experiment `git checkout` near-miss on `AsyncProcessRunner.swift`, not a battery, and `feature/planner-provider-router`'s is the `perl -0pi` mutation that corrupted UTF-8 punctuation — a case where the committed tree *saved* the branch, which is an argument for the guard rather than an instance of the hazard.
- **Cite this file by entry name, not by line number.** Every citation in this entry was first written as `path:line`, and every one was wrong within a day: entries are inserted at the top, so everything below them slides. The SONNY-83 incident alone sat at line **2946, then 2992, then 3038, then 3118** in `main` across three merges on 2026-08-18 — and this entry pushes it further down again, by however many lines this entry happens to be, which is the point and the reason no figure for it is given here. Two were: the first went stale when the entry was extended, the second when *this very bullet* was edited to add the first correction. The coordinator's independently-derived `:2992` for that same incident was accurate against `bdff514` and already stale against the `1002d82` that existed when the comment posted three minutes later — no carelessness involved, that is simply the shelf life of the form. Branch-entry names are stable and greppable, so this entry cites those instead.
- **The harness must not dirty the tree it just insisted on.** Logs go under `.build/mutate/<sha>-<timestamp>/`, and the fact that `.build/` is gitignored is checked with `git check-ignore` rather than assumed; a repository that does not ignore it gets its logs in a temp directory instead. The selftest's throwaway repo has no `.gitignore`, so the fallback path runs on every selftest. This was not foresight: the first selftest run failed on `?? .build/`, and every check after it failed too, because the harness's own logs tripped its own guard.
- **A plan file kept inside the working tree is an untracked file, and the harness will refuse its own plan.** Keep plans outside the tree. `--help` says so.
- **The mutation text is matched and patched as raw bytes by python3, never by a regex.** `feature/planner-provider-router`'s entry is the reason: a `perl -0pi` one-liner re-encoded UTF-8 punctuation across a file's doc comments and left a syntax error, mutating far more than it meant to.
- **A survivor is reported as a finding even when it is a deliberate neutrality check**, because the harness cannot know intent and the alternative is a plan-file field nobody needs. The dogfood battery's N1 — `!fullName.isEmpty` rewritten as `fullName.isEmpty == false` — survived exactly as designed, and it is a survivor in the report. Classifying it is the reader's job, as it was in the `feature/prebuilt-plan-dispatch` entry's own N1.
- **A compiler kill is recorded distinctly from a test kill.** The dogfood battery's D3 typed `period` as `Int`; nothing ran, so the run says "KILLED by the compiler — no test evidence." Folding that into a kill count inflates a battery's apparent strength, which is the same species of comfortable wrong answer the dirty-tree guard exists to stop.
- **Two harness bugs the selftest caught that reading did not.** `TEST_CMD` was referenced and never defined, and the resulting `set -u` death **exited 0** — a harness dying of its own bug while reporting success. **The cause stated here was wrong, and F6 in the fix round below has the real one:** it is the EXIT trap under bash 3.2, not the call site. `battery()` calling `exit` directly rather than returning through a `|| rc=$?` remains correct and load-bearing, but for a different hazard — a failing command *inside* `battery` being swallowed, and the run continuing to a summary built on a step that did not happen. And the interrupt check first passed vacuously: the stand-in suite signalled during the *baseline*, before anything was mutated, so "the mutant is gone" was trivially true; it now signals only once the mutant is in the file.
- **`git status --porcelain` was the right predicate, not a narrower one.** It covers staged, unstaged and untracked-but-not-ignored paths, all three of which mean the tree is not the commit the report will name. The selftest exercises the tracked and untracked cases separately.

Known limitations / deferred scope: **five review findings are recorded and left** per the coordinator's adjudication, written up in full on SONNY-75 — F3, nothing checks the tree after the baseline, so a suite that dirties it is reported against the first mutant instead; F4, the fallback log directory used when `.build/` is not gitignored is never removed, which only happens on the selftest path; F5, `--only ''` runs the whole battery and `--only M1,M1` reports M1 twice; a third near neighbour in this changelog, `feature/terminal-screen-check`'s dirty-tree rebase measurement, which the exclusion note above does not mention; and the "nothing in `Tests/` references `scripts/`" wording, imprecise rather than wrong, since `Tests/` carries `./scripts/plane` and `./scripts/deploy.sh` as redaction and shell-detection *fixtures* rather than functional references, so the substantive claim holds. Beyond those, the harness does not run mutants in parallel, does not support per-mutant test filters (use `MUTATE_TEST_CMD` with `--filter` for a whole run), and has no way to mark a mutant as expected-to-survive. All three were considered and left out under the ticket's explicit "do not over-build" instruction — a harness nobody adopts is worth less than a guard everybody hits. `WORKFLOW.md` still does not mention mutation testing; naming the harness in step 5's rigor bar is a candidate second discoverability surface and was left to the user rather than edited into the process doc unilaterally.

Open questions (required, write "none" if true): none.

Next branch: per the roadmap — this is out-of-band tooling and does not consume a roadmap row.

#### Fix round — PR #70 review, cycle 1 (fix commit `c84d516`; `d7678a4` before the rebase onto `4894fcb` replaced it)

**F6 — the "dies of its own bug while reporting success" mode was still live, and the change credited with fixing it governs something else.** This is the branch's own subject matter, which is why it leads. The diagnosis was re-derived from scratch before anything was built on it, on the bash this script actually runs under (`/bin/bash` 3.2.57): **a `set -u` death with no EXIT trap exits 1; with this script's trap shape it exits 0; and the usual remedy, a trap doing `rc=$?; trap - EXIT; exit $rc`, still exits 0** — because `$?` is already 0 by the time the trap runs. Injecting a single unbound-variable reference into a *copy* of the shipped script reproduced the whole failure: a normal-looking report, a death, exit 0. There is no status to preserve, so it has to be manufactured. A `MUTATE_EXIT_INTENDED` sentinel is set only by `finish()`; `assert_intended_exit` runs last in every EXIT trap and exits 1 when it was not set; every legitimate exit — `die`, both tree guards, the battery's 0 and 2, the signal handler's 130, the selftest's own two — goes through `finish`. Verified across the whole range: 0, 2, 7 and 130 all survive, and both a `set -u` and a `set -e` death now exit 1. **The plain `battery` call stays**, because the review confirmed it is load-bearing for a genuinely different hazard — with `|| rc=$?` restored and a failing `cp` injected inside `battery`, the failure is swallowed and the run reports a full summary and exits 2; called plainly it dies at exit 1 with no summary. Only the attribution was wrong, in the code comment and in the pitfall bullet above, and both now say what the call actually prevents.

**F1 — `git config status.showUntrackedFiles no` silently removed the untracked half of the guard**, with no edit to the script, in a script whose stated property is that it has no override. `--porcelain` honours that config. Both guards now read `git -c status.showUntrackedFiles=normal status --porcelain`.

**F2 — a `>>> file` path could point outside the repository, or at a gitignored path inside it.** It passed pre-flight, was mutated and restored, and the run printed `Summary at <sha>` over a file that SHA does not describe — and one `git status` can never see, so an interrupted run would leave that mutant somewhere the guard will never flag. Pre-flight now requires `git ls-files --error-unmatch` for every mutant file, which closes both cases with one check.

**F7 — the flagship dirty-tree selftest group was partly vacuous, and this entry cited it as evidence.** With `require_clean_tree` neutered outright, 2 of that group's 4 checks still passed and the untracked group passed *entirely*, because `require_clean_tree_after` also exits 1 and also prints the dirty path — just after both suites have already run against the dirty tree. The checks now assert the `refusing to run` wording only the pre-run guard emits, and reuse the existing sentinel file to assert no suite ran at all.

**F9 — "twice ... wrong in the reassuring direction" is once, and it was in three places.** A false *kill* is the dangerous direction: it claims coverage that is not there and the reader stops looking. A false *survivor* is an alarm — this script exits 2 for one — so it makes coverage look worse than it is and gets chased, which is what SONNY-83's did. Only SONNY-64's three bogus kills are reassuring-direction; SONNY-161's five and SONNY-83's one were survivors. Corrected at the header comment, the runtime refusal text (the most-read of the three, being what a person sees at the moment the guard fires) and `CLAUDE.md`. A repo-wide sweep for `reassuring` confirmed three sites and no fourth.

**Each fix was verified by removing it again — with one gap, found by the cycle-3 re-check and closed in G1 below.** Every one of the four with selftest coverage was deleted from a *copy* of the script and the copy's selftest re-run: the neutered guard produces 10 failures with the flagship group now among them, the missing `-c` flag 4, the disabled sentinel 2, the removed tracked-check 4. **What deleting the sentinel proved was that it must be present, not that it is in the right place**, and the EXIT trap's ordering turned out to be held by nothing at all. Five properties are now covered rather than four. The repository's own file was never modified during any of it. This is the discipline the branch exists to make routine, applied to the branch itself — and F6 is the argument for it, since the bug it fixes survived a full round precisely because nothing watched the sentinel fire.

**F8 was refuted by the review itself and nothing was changed for it.** The claim was that the `feature/prebuilt-plan-dispatch` entry carries no record of SONNY-64's incident. It does, at character 3,742 of a single 4,876-character paragraph, hashing identically at both SHAs. The transferable lesson is recorded on the ticket and is worth repeating here: **in this changelog an entry is a set of very long paragraphs, not a set of lines, so a grep hit is a pointer to a paragraph that then has to be read to its end.** Three separate searches hit that line and each stopped short of the incident, one at 900 characters and one at roughly 2,860.

#### Cycle-3 re-check — PR #70, round 4 (at `c7d5d22`)

Scoped by the founder to two findings. Three residuals — `assert_intended_exit` printing "exiting 1" while a signal death exits 128+N, the inconsistent output-disowning between SIGHUP and SIGINT/SIGTERM, and "two additions" describing one addition plus an in-place edit — are recorded and left.

**G1 — the EXIT trap's ordering was correct, load-bearing, and held by nothing.** `cleanup` must run before `assert_intended_exit`, or the exit ends the trap with the mutant still in the working tree. The comment said so; nothing tested it. The cause was structural rather than a missing assertion: the fault-injection seam sat before the baseline run, while `ACTIVE_FILE` first takes a value inside the mutant loop, so **the only death the selftest could inject landed at the one moment `cleanup` had nothing to restore**. Reproduced before fixing — reversing the trap on a copy leaves the mutant in the tree and never prints the restore message, and the selftest passed clean anyway, exit 0, 55 passes, zero failures. The seam now fires immediately after `apply_mutant` succeeds, and its group asserts the three things that only hold when cleanup runs first: the death landed with a mutant applied, the restore message printed, and the mutant is gone. Both directions, which is the acceptance the re-check set: **shipped order exits 0 with 58 checks and zero failures; reversed order exits 1 with five failures**, among them the mutant left in the tree and the tree left dirty. The other four deletion checks were re-run and reproduce exactly, so the move disturbed nothing.

**This is worth more than its size.** The property left uncovered was the one guarding the exact failure this branch exists to prevent — a mutant abandoned in a tree for someone to commit — inside a round whose own recorded standard was that each fix had been verified by removing it again. A seam placed one screen too early was enough to make a test that could never fail look like a test that passed.

**G2 — the Tests line called `5064e22` "the last commit that touches code", and `5064e22` changes the changelog only.** The last commit touching `scripts/mutate` was `c84d516`, two earlier. The sentence also contradicted itself, defining everything after `5064e22` as records-only by a test `5064e22` itself fails. **This is the third time the same treadmill has caught this entry**, and the shape is worth recording because it is not carelessness: the wording it replaced was accurate when written and merely went stale, and the replacement was durable in form but false in content — a descriptor chosen to stop going stale, which stopped being true instead. The fix is to stop describing the SHA and state the property the figures actually depend on, in a form that a change invalidating the figures also makes visibly false.

### Branch: docs/sonny-168-force-push-clause
Status: complete
Date: 2026-08-18
Tickets: SONNY-168 (CLAUDE.md's history rule contradicts WORKFLOW.md's force-push authorization). One clause. Not a new rule — a pointer to one that already exists.
Reviewed by: fresh session (per WORKFLOW.md step 7), PR #71, cycle 1 — findings relayed by the coordinator, since the reviewing session was retired before posting them. **F1 fixed**: the clause narrowed the prohibition further than `WORKFLOW.md` authorizes. **F3 fixed**: a blanket claim in this entry, below. **F4 fixed** as a dated append on the PR body. **F2 recorded, deliberately not fixed** — see the last bullet under known limitations.

Spec sections covered: none. A process-record fix.
Files changed: `CLAUDE.md` (one bullet in Conventions), and this changelog. **`WORKFLOW.md` is deliberately untouched** — it was already correct, and this ticket exists because the auto-loaded file contradicted it in emphasis, not because the rule was wrong.
Tests: **not run, under WORKFLOW.md's one rerun exemption** — "a diff provably confined to docs/comments may skip the rerun — anything touching `Sources/` or `Tests/` never skips." Proven rather than asserted: `git diff --name-only` reports `CLAUDE.md` and this changelog, and zero paths under `Sources/` or `Tests/`. No test reads either file; the handful of `CLAUDE.md` mentions in the tree are doc comments citing its rules, not code depending on its text.

Behavior added: none. Documentation only.

Behavior preserved (required, no blanket claims):
- **The authorization itself is unchanged**, because CLAUDE.md never granted it — `WORKFLOW.md`'s merge-one-branch-at-a-time rule did, and still does, as the sole source.
- **The merge gate is untouched.** "Merging is the user's, always" leads the clause exactly as before.
- **The authorization is untouched, and it is the only thing here that could have been.** It lives in `WORKFLOW.md`, which this branch does not edit; `CLAUDE.md` never granted it. So nothing about what a session may actually do changed in either direction.
- **The prohibition's scope is deliberately *not* claimed as preserved.** An earlier draft of this entry said "the prohibition is untouched in substance", under the heading that forbids blanket claims, while the first draft of the clause had changed its scope from absolute to `main`-and-other-branches — which was the whole of what moved (PR #71 review, F3). The shipped clause restores the prohibition to absolute, so it now *is* untouched; the claim was false about the draft it described, and is left corrected rather than quietly made true by the later fix.

Architectural decisions / pitfalls discovered (required):
- **The defect was reading order, not rule content.** `CLAUDE.md` is auto-loaded into every session; `WORKFLOW.md` is opened on purpose. So the absolute-sounding sentence was the one every session saw by default, and the exception lived in a file it might not have read yet. A session following the letter of the auto-loaded file would refuse to finish an instructed rebase — worse than the outcome the rule guards against.
- **Two independent readers made the same mistake from the same text**, which is what earns a clause rather than a note: PR #69's implementing session flagged its own authorized force-push as a possible rule break, and the coordinator then proposed adding a carve-out that already existed. Both had read only the auto-loaded sentence.
- **The clause says "already authorized rather than granted here", deliberately.** The risk in fixing this is that `CLAUDE.md` starts reading like a second source of authorization that could drift from `WORKFLOW.md`. Naming it a pointer, and naming the rule it points at, keeps one source.
- **The agreement was checked clause by clause rather than by impression.** Every constraint in `WORKFLOW.md`'s rule has a counterpart in the new text: own ticket branch only; arising from the rebase; always `--force-with-lease`; never bare `--force`; never another branch; never `main`. Nothing in the new text has no counterpart there, which is the direction that would mean widening.
- **Narrowing a prohibition is not the same as carving an exception out of it, and the first draft did the former while claiming the latter** (PR #71 review, F1). Scoping the sentence to "`main` or any branch that is not the session's own ticket branch" left own-branch history rewriting *by other means* — squash, amend, dropping a pushed commit — prohibited by neither file: `WORKFLOW.md` authorizes only the force-push that follows a rebase and says nothing about the rest, so the draft moved those from prohibited to unaddressed. **The tell is redundancy**: if the prohibition already excludes own-branch work, then "the force-push is the exception" is not an exception to anything. One of the two constructions had to be doing nothing, and that is the symptom worth remembering — when a carve-out reads as redundant with the rule it sits under, the rule has usually been narrowed by accident.
- **The defective wording came from the ticket's own proposed replacement**, written by the coordinator, and was implemented as contracted. Recorded because the lesson is about where to look: a ticket that hands over exact wording moves the drafting decision upstream, and a session following it faithfully cannot catch a defect in it by being careful.

Known limitations / deferred scope:
- **`CLAUDE.md`'s Conventions bullet is now longer**, and length is the tax on it being the file everyone reads by default. Accepted: the alternative is the shorter sentence that was wrong twice.

- **F2, recorded and deliberately not fixed: `CLAUDE.md` says "a rebase" where `WORKFLOW.md` keys its authorization to the post-merge rebase specifically.** So the clause reads very slightly broader than the rule it points at, and that is the one constraint whose counterpart is partial rather than exact. **Left as is on purpose.** Narrowing it to the post-merge rebase would leave a session rebasing for another legitimate reason — a stale branch, an instructed rebase outside the merge sequence — with no authorization at all, which opens a new gap rather than closing one. `WORKFLOW.md` itself grounds the authorization in "the same standing authorization as regular pushes", which is scoped by *branch* rather than by *reason*, so the broader reading is the one consistent with its basis. **Written down so the next reader does not "fix" this into existence.**

Open questions (required): none.

Next branch: not a roadmap row. A one-clause records fix. Rows D, E, J and 12 are unaffected.

**Founder decisions of 2026-08-16 (Sauransh Bhardwaj), full text on SONNY-14's comments of that date.** All are implemented here unless noted:
- **The list shows 30 days and search reaches past it.** Nothing is deleted by age. The two ship together on purpose — shortening the window without search would strand every older task with no way to reach it.

- **Clipboard history pauses** for the duration of a suppressed run, with the cost accepted knowingly: text the user copies by hand during that task is not saved either.

**The 30-day figure is ratified as of 2026-08-16, not 2026-08-01.** The "30-day retention decision recorded 2026-08-01" cited by this row's original scoping **has no recorded content anywhere** — not in this changelog, `docs/sonny-major-release-spec.md`, `docs/sonny-founder-design-decisions.md`, git history (`git log -S`), or any reachable Plane ticket. Every documentary hit for the phrase lands on the vision provider's unrelated 30-day retention at OpenCode/OpenAI, which is a third party's storage and a different number entirely. Recorded here to stop the dead citation reaching a third document.

**Cycle-4 round (PR #67), three corrections, no production behaviour changed.** (1) The tie test added in cycle 3 was **flaky by construction**: it sampled `Date()` once and let the run stamp its own row about twenty milliseconds later, so the rows tied only when no second boundary fell between — roughly one run in fifty failed, and on the setup assertion rather than the behaviour. It now seeds a band of four consecutive seconds so a tie holds wherever the run lands, plus a band thirty seconds ahead so the mutation's failure is deterministic rather than merely likely. Its own comment, which claimed the test "still passes" if the tie stopped holding, was wrong about its own assertion and is corrected. (2) and (3) are the two false claims corrected under Known limits below — what the suite cannot reach, and which publish site is unpinned. Both were mine, both were stated confidently, and both are corrected on the record rather than edited away.

**Cycle-3 round (PR #67), two production defects in F4's own fix, both fixed here.** Defect A: the task-detail request was answered inside `TasksFoundationView`, which exists only while the Tasks page is selected — so a notification click from Insights, Routines or Workspaces brought the window forward and opened nothing, and left the request set, so arriving at Tasks afterwards did not fire it either (`onChange` does not fire for a value that did not change while the view was mounted). The request is now answered above the page switch: it selects Tasks, and the page consumes it from `onAppear` as well as `onChange`. `selection` gains **no second writer** — the sidebar's assignment became `select(_:)` and both callers go through it. Defect B: the notice's `taskID` was re-derived as `taskHistoryRecords.first?.id`. That is unsound, not merely fragile — `completedAt` persists at whole-second resolution, so two runs finishing in the same second compare equal, and `sorted(by:)` is not stable, so the head can be the earlier row and the notification names the wrong task. **The same whole-second truncation `CompletedTaskRecord.id` exists to defeat (SONNY-115), re-entering through the phrase "the most recent row."** The re-derivation is removed rather than hardened: `recordTaskHistoryIfTerminal` returns the id it wrote and the call sites hand it down.

**Pre-merge review round (PR #67), seven findings, all resolved before merge.** F1: the vision journal's suppression decision was pinned by nothing — it lived inline in a function no test here can execute, so a mutation handing the store over regardless of policy survived the whole suite; extracted to `visionSessionJournalStoreForThisRun` and asserted, and that mutation now dies. F2: the scheduled executor inherited this run's policy, so a foreground run paused at a clarification could suppress a scheduled routine's Shortcut run history while its task-history row was still written; `.record` is now passed explicitly. F3: an abandoned clarification leaves clipboard history paused — **not fixed, see Known limits**, because closing it needs a control that does not exist. F4: a finished-run notification opened the widget, which renders nothing for a Command-Center-origin result; it now opens that task's detail dialog, per the founder's decision of 2026-08-17. F5: the Insights half of `searchingDoesNotMoveAnyInsightsNumber` compared a pure function to itself. F6: a vacuous expectation. F7: this entry undercounted its own new test files and stamped its count with a stale SHA — both corrected above.

Behavior added:
- **`CompletedTaskRecord.id`**, Optional per the twice-documented decode rule, defaulted to a fresh UUID and backfilled on load for every record written before it existed. A failed backfill rewrite is not a load failure: the records come back anyway, the file is left byte-identical, and it retries next load.
- **Per-record delete in both stores**, plus a view-model delete that removes everything hanging off a row *before* the row.
- **Two delete actions in Command Center** — a footer button and a row context menu for the whole task, and a section-level action for the screen record alone. Both confirm first.
- **Search over task history**, matching the command text and the workspace name, case- and diacritic-insensitively.
- **"Don't save this task"** — a per-task widget switch, off by default, reset after every task, reachable only before dispatch.
- **The notification gate opens.** `SonnyAttention.isUserWorkingInSonny` replaces `isAnySonnySurfaceVisible`.
- **A finished Command-Center-originated run posts its summary**, and **a notified outcome persists** until the user retries or submits something else.

Behavior preserved (required, no blanket claims):
- **Neither cap moved.** `TaskHistoryStore.maxItems` is still 10,000 and `VisionSessionJournalStore.maxSessions` still 500. `maxItems` became injectable (SONNY-161) with the default unchanged, and a new test pins the shipped value and that no production path overrides it.
- **The 30-day window is display-only.** Insights' stats, streak and week maths, the workspace breakdown and the per-workspace counts all read the un-windowed store, before and after a query is typed — asserted directly.
- **An outcome that was *not* notified auto-clears exactly as before.** That timer exists because a banner surviving repeated collapses on a permanent overlay was a real reported bug.
- **The widget's origin gate is not dropped.** Its progress half is still live.

**The record-identity finding, and the second time this truncation has bitten.** `CompletedTaskRecord` had no id, so the Tasks page faked one twice — `TaskLogEntry.id` as `"\(startedAt.timeIntervalSince1970)-\(command)"` and the list's `ForEach(id: \.startedAt)`. Both are `(command, startedAt)` compound keys, and the store persists dates with plain `.iso8601`, which truncates to whole seconds — so two runs of one command started inside the same second are indistinguishable, and a delete built on that key can take the wrong twin. **This is the second time whole-second ISO8601 truncation has broken a key in this repository**: the deleted egress ledger replaced the same `startedAt` join after mutation E10 survived its battery. Read that entry's own PR #49 correction (F6) alongside it, which records the E10 sentence as overstated — so the precedent is that this key was abandoned here once for this reason, not that it is on record as having corrupted data. This branch does not rely on the precedent: the collision is constructed and asserted in `TaskHistoryDeletionTests`.
Also checked and rejected on the merits: widening the timestamp. Measured on this repo's toolchain at `4a7d996` (Apple Swift 6.3.3), `JSONDecoder`'s `.iso8601` strategy reads fractional seconds back fine, so the migration would survive — it is the wrong fix because `(command, startedAt)` stays a *natural* key at any precision.

**The caps position, and the deliberate differential lifetime.** The founder's instruction was raise them, surface them, or state the limit. Stating is the only one that costs nothing: raising is paid on every finished task (`record(_:)` decodes and re-encrypts the whole file), and surfacing would be the forbidden how-it-works copy. Measured at `36cef9e`: a history at the cap is 3.53 MiB and one `record(_:)` call is **130 ms** median; at row E's projected record size it is 38.81 MiB and **307 ms** — eleven times the file for 2.4 times the time, because encryption and I/O dominate. The journal's 500 sessions against task history's 10,000 means the sensitive half expires far sooner than the row it hangs off; that started as a side effect and is now **deliberate**, with the consequence built rather than only written: a screen record that aged out and one the user deleted are indistinguishable, because the product cannot tell them apart without explaining itself.

**No notification had ever fired, and why the usual proof was not enough.** All four triggers were gated on `!isAnySonnySurfaceVisible`, which is `widgetController.isVisible || commandCenterWindow?.isKeyWindow == true`; the widget is shown at launch and `FloatingWidgetWindowController.hide()` has zero callers. That reasoning has a hole worth recording: an `NSPanel` whose `hidesOnDeactivate` is `true` goes invisible whenever the app deactivates, which would have opened the gate every time the user switched apps with no `hide()` call anywhere. It was **measured** rather than assumed — a throwaway program building the panel with the same `[.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel]` style mask reports `hidesOnDeactivate = false`, and the property is never set in `Sources/`. So the gate really was permanently closed, by a stronger route than enumeration alone. The subscriptions were *wired* and had never *fired*; SONNY-56 replaced the gate with the founder's rule of 2026-08-17, **ratified by him on that date** after the coordinator could not confirm the original attribution (SONNY-56's ratification comment records why that matters more than the rule itself).

Known limits (recorded, not solved):
- **macOS's own Notification Center is outside "Don't save this task".** An approval or error notification delivered during a suppressed run is retained by the system, not by Sonny. It may not be explained in the product.
- **The provider still sees the command.** Suppression is about what is stored, never what is sent. The server-side never-retain half is row 12's.
- **A suppressed run that goes wrong cannot be diagnosed**, because nothing was kept. That is the feature working, accepted explicitly on 2026-08-16.
- **Delete is local-only until row 12 lands the server half.** Under the 2026-08-16 no-staged-release directive nothing reaches a user before both exist; the condition is recorded on SONNY-106.
- **A suppressed run earns no Shortcut trust** — `hasCleanObservedSuccess` feeds risk tiering, so a suppressed run may cost an extra confirmation later. The right direction: suppression must never buy a quieter approval.
- **Defect A is a view-mounting change and no test here reaches it.** The suite was green while the defect was live, and stays green with the fix reverted. **The reason first recorded here — "this repository constructs no views" — was false**, and is corrected rather than quietly dropped: `ProductShellTests` constructs `CommandCenterView` and `FloatingWidgetView` at **eight sites**. What no test does is *evaluate a view's body or drive its lifecycle*, and that is the real limit — `onAppear`, `onChange` and the page switch never run, so the wiring inside them is unreachable whether or not the value is constructed. For this view there is a second, harder barrier: `TasksFoundationView` is `private`, so it is file-scoped and cannot be named from a test even through `@testable`. What guards it is the manual item below, which had to be sharpened to start from a page *other* than Tasks: as originally written it would have passed with the defect present, the second time on this branch a manual item could not reach the defect it was meant to cover. The same standing limit as SONNY-25's collapse wiring.
- **Only one of the notice's two publish sites is pinned.** The battery below kills a mutation that drops the id at the ordinary success site, and one that drops it at the second site **survives** — the code there is correct; what is missing is the test. **That site is `performApproval`, so the unpinned path is resume-after-*approval*, not resume-after-clarification as first recorded here.** The correction matters because the two are not the same path and the mistake pointed at one that is already covered: `performApproval` is reached only from `approvePendingRun`, while a clarification answer goes back through `start()` and so through `performStart` — the first publish site, which the battery kills. Closing it needs a test that pauses a run at an approval and approves it. Recorded on SONNY-121 rather than built, because the founder scoped this round to the two defects alone.
- **An abandoned clarification leaves clipboard history paused until relaunch.** A run paused for a clarification is still running, so "Don't save this task" correctly stays on and the clipboard stays paused — but **no surface can abandon that pause**: the widget's clarification panel offers only Submit, the composer is disabled by `isTaskInFlight`, and `canCancel` is `isAwaitingApproval || (isRunning && currentTask != nil)`, both false there. The only ways out are answering it, wiping local data, or relaunching, and monitoring is restored from settings at launch. Found by PR #67's review (F3) and **deliberately not fixed in that round**: closing it needs a cancel or dismiss affordance on the clarification panel, which is a product decision and SONNY-109's surface. Written to SONNY-120 as a stop-and-report.
- **`scheduledRunNotice` still renders on one surface.** SONNY-113's root cause (the dead gate) is fixed; its second half is not, and that ticket stays open for the founder to triage.

**Wireframe exception, per CLAUDE.md's rule.** No Tasks-page or task-detail wireframe exists in this repository — verified, not inherited: `docs/wireframes/` contains exactly one file, `15-SegmentedControl.svg`, and a repo-wide search for any `.svg` or `.png` outside `.build` returns that one file and nothing else. Every surface this branch adds is therefore net-new System A built on session judgment, with SONNY-109 as where it gets designed properly. The judgment calls it carries, listed so the pass has them: the row delete is a context menu rather than a trailing button; the "Don't save this task" control is a third circular button that widens the composer row by 48pt; the two delete labels and both confirmation messages are proposals.

Architectural decisions / pitfalls discovered:
- **A rule the compiler and the suite both check beats a list.** `LocalStore.kind` switches with no `default`, so a new store cannot compile unclassified, and a test matches every case against `LocalDataDeletionService.defaultStoreFileURLs()`, so a new store file cannot arrive unclassified either. Row 12's tenth store is meant to fail both loudly.
- **Withhold the store rather than check a flag.** Where a seam existed — `AgentRunner`'s Optional recent-artifacts store, row I's Optional journal store — suppression passes `nil` instead of guarding a writer. Only Shortcut run history needed a guard, and it sits at the one helper wrapping all three writes.
- **A "byte-identical after a suppressed run" test can pass for the wrong reason.** The acceptance test enumerates all five trace stores, but the fixture's planner has no command that generates an artifact or invokes a Shortcut, so two of five were trivially unchanged either way. Only a mutation battery found it; both are now pinned at their own seams.
- **Pausing a poller is not the same as suppressing it.** `ClipboardHistoryMonitor.poll()` records whenever the pasteboard's change count differs from the last one it saw, and that counter survives a pause — so the first poll after a suppressed run recorded exactly the text the pause existed to withhold. Measured before fixing. `resynchronize()` closes it.
- **There is no single `defer` covering every terminal state.** `cancelCurrentRun()` has none and is the app-wide deny entry point; the two that exist also fire for approval and clarification *pauses*. Anything that must happen once per finished run is a guarded call at each terminal point, not one `defer`.
- **The pass/fail probe could not resolve a 2%-of-CPU change.** SONNY-161's filing claimed the eviction tests caused `VisionSessionRunTests`' flakiness; measured under controlled load, `origin/main` failed too and the results inverted at a lower load. Total suite CPU moved consistently where pass rates did not. The real fix was SONNY-160's deadlines, and SONNY-161's own diagnosis is corrected on that ticket.
- **`everyAgentViewModelStoredPropertyIsClassifiedAgainstTheLocalDataWipe` caught real state three times running** — the search query, the outcome notice and the notified marker — and each answer was a behaviour question rather than bookkeeping. The last one is a real bug it prevented: a stale marker would have made the wipe's own completion message un-collapsible.
- **The suite pins rules; the wiring that delivers them is often manual.** Mutations of `FloatingWidgetView`'s collapse decision, `AppDelegate`'s marking call and the notification's default action all survive, because nothing here constructs a view or an app delegate. That is the standing gap SONNY-25 recorded, restated rather than rediscovered.

Records corrected on this branch (each was wrong before row D and is named so the correction is auditable):
- `TaskHistoryDisplayWindow.swift` said `TaskHistoryStore` "keeps every record", that consumers see "the complete, un-windowed history", and that deletion is "always an explicit, user-initiated action, never automatic". All three false — the store evicts oldest-first, automatically and silently.
- `CommandCenterView.swift`'s `displayedRecords` said Insights "still sees the complete history". Same error, narrower.
- `.claude/rules/macagent-ui-conventions.md` said the widget's origin gate avoids a duplicate "progress/result" panel. Only the progress half is live; corrected to `progress`, paragraph otherwise intact.
- `TaskLogEntry`'s comment said a collision needs two records "starting in the same instant". It is the same *second*.

### Branch: fix/sonny-145-click-point-centre
Status: complete
Date: 2026-08-18
Tickets: SONNY-145 (vision click points map to a pixel's leading edge rather than its centre — a systematic up-left bias of up to one sent pixel). Filed by the SONNY-114 session; the ticket offered "do nothing" as a reasonable outcome and the founder assigned the fix instead.
Reviewed by: fresh session (per WORKFLOW.md step 7), PR #69, cycle 1. Verdict: **the mapping is correct and no behaviour defect was found**; all three findings were precision in the record, one of them also costing two assertions' worth of test code. G1 a wrong characterisation of the old sweep's sampling, G2 two mutation kill counts understated, G3 a direction claim true of x and silent about y. All three fixed in a records-and-mechanical round; see the fix-round section at the end of this entry.

Spec sections covered: none new. A correctness fix inside row I's acting loop.
Files changed: `Sources/MacAgentCore/ScreenActionSynthesizer.swift` (the mapping and its doc comment). `Tests/MacAgentCoreTests/VisionDecisionAndGeometryTests.swift` (five exact-point expectations, and the ladder sweep). `Tests/MacAgentTests/VisionSessionRunTests.swift` (the end-to-end resampled-click test). This changelog. Four paths.
Tests: CLAUDE.md's exact flagged command -> pass, **1290 tests in 95 suites**, exit 0, at `84b378f` — the last commit on this branch that touches code; every commit after it changes records only. Branch point `bdff514` measured on this branch: **1290 in 95** — **+0 tests, +0 suites**, correctly: this branch tightens and re-points existing tests rather than adding any.

> **Re-stamped after the rebase onto `bdff514`.** The branch first recorded **1289 in 95** over a 1289 branch point at `64e4d20`, at SHAs the rebase replaced; `fix/sonny-102-termius-deny-list` then merged and added one test, moving the branch point to 1290. **Both ends were measured again rather than adjusted arithmetically**, and the delta is still +0 — the figure moved because the branch point moved, not because this branch added anything. `git range-diff 64e4d20..efb283b bdff514..HEAD` reports the code commit and the fix-round commit **identical**, with the one changed commit differing only by where the changelog entry lands, which is the conflict resolution itself.

Behavior added:
- A model-named pixel resolves to that pixel's **centre**. Every synthesized click moves down-and-right by half a sent pixel — half a point at full resolution, one point at the ladder's 0.5 floor — and the systematic up-left bias is gone.

Behavior preserved (required, no blanket claims):
- **The sent size is still the one answer about how big the picture is** (SONNY-114). The half-pixel is added *before* scaling, so it is half of the model's own pixel and inherits `sentImageSize` rather than introducing a second opinion. `aResampledCaptureResolvesItsClickThroughTheSizeTheModelWasShown` still runs end to end through the real runner, and the mutation below shows what would break if this were written as a fixed point offset.
- **The fresh-frame policy.** A window that moved still resolves at its new origin; a window that resized is still refused for a recapture; a vanished window still ends the action. Untouched.
- **Own-window suppression.** A click landing inside Sonny's own window is still refused — asserted at the new coordinate, since the fixture's suppression rectangle contains both.
- **Bounds checking.** `isInsideImage` is untouched and still `0 <= x < sentPixelWidth`. A centre-sampled point cannot leave the window either: the largest resolves to half a sent pixel inside the trailing edge rather than exactly on it.

Architectural decisions / pitfalls discovered (required):
- **The half is expressed in sent pixels, not points, and that is the whole SONNY-114 interaction.** `(i + 0.5) * scale` is half of the model's pixel; `i * scale + 0.5` is half of a point and would mean the correction stopped tracking the resample. A mutation writing it the second way fails three tests including the end-to-end one, so the constraint is enforced rather than merely intended.
- **The ladder sweep was sampling sub-pixel positions degenerately.** Distinct fractional positions within a sent pixel is exactly `steps / gcd(sentDimension, steps)`. Over a 1440x900 window at 144 steps, by rung and axis: 1.0 → x 1, y 4; 0.8 → x 1, y 1; 0.64 → **x 72**, y 1; 0.5 → x 1, y 8. **Five of the eight cells reach exactly one position** — always a pixel boundary, precisely where leading-edge and centre sampling agree — and only three sample more. The step count is now **997**: prime and coprime with every sent dimension here (1440, 900, 1152, 720, 922, 576, 450), so every `gcd` is 1 and every cell becomes 997.
- **`x` at scale 0.64 is the outlier at 72, and it is the cell that mattered** (PR #69 review, G1). An earlier draft of this entry said "2 to 8 distinct positions" for the non-degenerate cells, which missed the single cell where the old sweep's ability to see this defect actually sat — half its targets at distinct positions. The conclusion held; the number attached to it did not.
- **The table is exact rational arithmetic, and that is not a detail.** Recomputing it in the `Double` arithmetic the test itself uses returns larger, unstable counts (8, 129, 14…), because a fraction that is mathematically 0 appears as a scatter around 1e-14. Any count taken from that depends on how much rounding dust the counter tolerates — which is why the first tally, the review's table and a re-run all disagreed until it was derived exactly.
- **The tempting stronger claim about that is false, and was measured rather than assumed.** "The old sweep could not have caught the bias" was written into a doc comment and then removed: running the new assertions against the pre-fix mapping *with the step count back at 144* still fails. What 144 bought was a test whose discriminating power sat in a few rung/axis pairs by arithmetic accident, one ladder change away from resting on nothing — which is worth fixing, and is a smaller claim than the one first written.
- **The direction assertions are belt-and-braces, not load-bearing, and this entry first claimed the opposite** (PR #69 review, G3). For a constant offset `c` in sent pixels the signed residual spans `[-c, 1-c)` pixels, so requiring `|residual| <= 0.5` pixels forces `c = 0.5` exactly — **the half-pixel bound alone already pins the offset, direction included**. "A bound alone cannot pin a direction" was true of the *one*-sent-pixel bound this branch replaced and is not true of the bound that replaced it. The assertions are kept because they are cheap, they document intent, and they still say something about a mapping that is not a constant offset.
- **They are tracked per axis, and the obvious two-line fix does not work.** Fed from `signedX` alone, the claim was true of x and silent about y. ORing `signedY` into the same two flags does not fix it either — x on its own still sets both, so removing `+ 0.5` from y alone still fires the assertion **zero** times. Measured both ways before choosing; four per-axis flags are what makes the claim true, and the y-only mutation then fires it once.

Known limitations / deferred scope:
- **The suite establishes the arithmetic and nothing beyond it.** Whether a click lands on the control the user actually sees is not something anything in this repository can drive — no agent can operate the real macOS app — so no test here is evidence of real-world aiming accuracy, and none claims to be.
- **This change is not manually verifiable as an improvement either, and that is stated rather than papered over.** The correction is 0.5 to 1 point on controls that are at least 20 points on their short edge. Nobody watching an attended run can tell 200 from 201. The manual item below is therefore a **regression check** — that the acting loop still clicks what it means to — and it cannot confirm the fix works, because the defect it fixes was never observable at that resolution either. The case for the change is that the error was real, directional, and free to remove, not that anyone had seen it.
- **The model's own aim is untouched by this.** Whether a model aims as well at a resampled picture is SONNY-114's attended question and stays open.

**PR #69 review — three findings, all record precision, none a behaviour defect.**

- **G1 (fixed).** The "2 to 8 distinct positions" characterisation of the old 144-step sweep was wrong about the one cell that mattered: x at scale 0.64 had **72**. Re-derived here from `steps / gcd(sentDimension, steps)` rather than taken from the review, and the exact table replaces the prose estimate. It also showed something the review's own table did not: **five** of the eight cells are fully degenerate, not two, because three cells the float computation reports as "2" are mathematically 1 plus rounding dust.
- **G2 (fixed).** Both mutation kill counts were understated — 7 not 6 for the leading-edge revert, 4 not 3 for the fixed half point. **The cause is one thing, not two off-by-ones:** both were counted from a `--filter 'VisionDecisionAndGeometryTests'` run, which cannot see `Tests/MacAgentTests`, and were then written as though they were full-suite figures. The missing kill in each case is the end-to-end `aResampledCaptureResolvesItsClickThroughTheSizeTheModelWasShown`, plus `aRetinaScaledCaptureMapsThroughItsOwnDerivedScale` for the half-point mutation. Re-measured on the full suite.
- **G3 (fixed, and the prescribed fix did not work).** `sawUndershoot`/`sawOvershoot` were both computed from `signedX`, so the direction claim was true of x and silent about y. The review prescribed two lines ORing `signedY` into the same flags; **measured, that fires the assertion zero times**, because x on its own still sets both. Four per-axis flags are what satisfies the review's own N3 acceptance. The rationale is corrected too: with a half-sent-pixel bound the offset is already forced to exactly 0.5, so the direction assertions are belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing, and the old wording described the one-pixel bound this branch replaced.
- **A note on counting from console output.** The review quoted the y-bound assertion firing 2456 times under the y-only mutation; re-runs of the identical configuration here produced 2407, 2451 and 2461. A grep over test-console output is not a stable counter for a high-volume assertion. The stable, binary figure is the one the acceptance rests on: the both-directions assertion fires **0** times before the fix and **1** after.

Open questions (required): none. The ticket offered "do nothing" as a legitimate outcome; the fix was assigned instead, and this entry is the record of that rather than of a silent choice.

Next branch: not a roadmap row. An out-of-row correctness fix in row I's acting loop, sequenced ahead of the implementation lanes because it is small and its decision was already made. Rows D, E, J and 12 are unaffected.

Eight paths, which is what `git diff --name-only 64e4d20...HEAD` reports.
